common_name: Mini Skirt Hosta (Miniature Blue-Green Variegated Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Mini Skirt is a Hans Hansen introduction that arose as a sport of Mighty Mouse and stays true-miniature in scale.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Mini Skirt is the 2024 American Hosta Growers Association Hosta of the Year, a true miniature that arose as a sport of 'Mighty Mouse' and forms a tight mound of thick, wavy-margined leaves with blue-green centers and creamy yellow edges that lighten to creamy white by summer as the center greens up. The heavy leaf substance gives good resistance to slug damage despite the plant's diminutive size. Pale lavender flowers rise on short scapes just above the foliage in early summer. Its small scale suits containers, fairy gardens, troughs, and the front edge of a shaded border.

common_name: Primo Wild Rose Heuchera (Large Rosy Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Primo Wild Rose is part of a heuchera breeding line selected for unusually large, substantial leaves and vigorous garden performance.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; good drainage combined with steady moisture keeps the crown from rotting while preventing the plant from drying out in summer heat. Primo Wild Rose produces large, vibrant rosy purple leaves as part of a Primo breeding line selected for bigger, more substantial foliage and sturdier garden performance than many older, smaller-leaved heuchera cultivars. It thrives from shade to part shade and draws butterflies and hummingbirds while resisting deer browsing. Small flower spikes appear above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the season-long leaf color and texture. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Primo Pretty Pistachio Heuchera (Large Chartreuse-Lime Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in filtered sun to partial shade; Pretty Pistachio is part of the Primo breeding line selected for unusually large, substantial leaves and vigorous garden performance.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in filtered sun or partial shade; too much direct sun bleaches the bright leaf color while deep shade dulls it, so dappled light gives the best foliage display. Primo Pretty Pistachio emerges chartreuse in spring and mellows to lime green through summer, with large, substantial leaves typical of the Primo breeding line, which are bigger and more vigorous than the related Dolce series. Huge five-inch-wide clusters of medium pink flowers appear continuously from midsummer into early fall and dry on the stems to a raspberry color. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Little Cuties Coco Heuchera (Miniature Dark Chocolate Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Coco is a Terra Nova miniature heuchera bred for its dark chocolate foliage and diminutive scale in containers and small garden pockets.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Coco is a diminutive coral bells cultivar in the Terra Nova Little Cuties series, described as a miniature of 'Obsidian', forming a tight mound of rounded, lobed leaves in dark cherry-brown to near-black tones that shift somewhat with season and light exposure. Its dwarf scale and multiple crowns make it well suited to rock garden pockets, trough plantings, and the front edge of a shaded border where a standard-sized heuchera would crowd out neighbors. Slender stems carry light pink bell flowers well above the foliage from late spring into fall. Keep soil evenly moist and sharply drained, and divide congested crowns every two to three years in spring to keep the mound tight and vigorous.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries — Heuchera Little Cuties Series
North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Little Cuties Ginger Snap Heuchera (Miniature Rosy Tan-Brown Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Ginger Snap is a Terra Nova miniature heuchera bred for its rosy tan-brown foliage and diminutive scale in containers and small garden pockets.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Ginger Snap is a diminutive coral bells cultivar in the Terra Nova Little Cuties series, forming a tight low mound of small, lobed leaves in rosy and tan-brown tones. Its dwarf scale and multiple crowns make it well suited to rock garden pockets, trough plantings, and the front edge of a shaded border where a standard-sized heuchera would crowd out neighbors. Rose-pink flower spikes rise well above the foliage from late spring into fall, drawing bees and small pollinators over a long season. Keep soil evenly moist and sharply drained, and divide congested crowns every two to three years in spring to keep the mound tight and vigorous.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries — Heuchera Little Cuties Series

common_name: Little Cuties Sweet Tart Heuchera (Miniature Chartreuse-Lime Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Sweet Tart is a Terra Nova miniature heuchera, introduced in 2012, bred for its chartreuse-to-lime foliage and diminutive scale in containers and small garden pockets.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Little Cuties Sweet Tart is a diminutive coral bells cultivar in the Terra Nova Little Cuties series, forming a tight mound of small, crinkled, lobed leaves that emerge chartreuse in spring and settle to lime green for the rest of the season. Its dwarf scale and multiple crowns make it well suited to rock garden pockets, trough plantings, and the front edge of a shaded border where a standard-sized heuchera would crowd out neighbors. Bicolor cerise and hot pink flowers rise on dark, wand-like stems well above the foliage from spring through fall. Keep soil evenly moist and sharply drained, and divide congested crowns every two to three years in spring to keep the mound tight and vigorous.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries — Heuchera Little Cuties Series

common_name: Dolce Toffee Tart Heuchera (Ginger-Caramel Silver-Overlay Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with protection from full sun, which can bleach its light-toned foliage; Toffee Tart is part of the Proven Winners Dolce series bred for compact habit and rich foliage color.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, avoiding full sun which can bleach the light foliage color. Dolce Toffee Tart displays shifting shades of ginger caramel through the season: new spring leaves emerge amber with a silvery overlay, mature to ginger with silver overlay through summer, and settle to green by late summer. Creamy white flowers are held on contrasting burgundy stems from late spring into summer. Part of the Proven Winners Dolce series, it forms a dense, compact mound well suited to containers and the front of a shaded border. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: Proven Winners — Dolce Series Coral Bells

common_name: Dolce Appletini Heuchera (Lime-Green Silver-Overlay Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Dolce Appletini is part of the Proven Winners Dolce series bred for compact habit and rich foliage color.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; morning sun with afternoon shade keeps the foliage color richest. Dolce Appletini forms a dense mound of medium-sized lime green leaves with a silvery overlay, contrasted by dark rose-red stems carrying rich ruby-red flowers in mid-summer that draw butterflies and hummingbirds while resisting deer. Part of the Proven Winners Dolce series, it is salt tolerant and spreads wider than many other Dolce cultivars. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: Proven Winners — Dolce Series Coral Bells
